content:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: *INCIDENT* `HOSTED-5XX` triggered
Service: hosted-inference
Signal: 5xx_rate_high
Route: `acct_4f2c / routes/chat-prod`
Region: `us-east-1`
Current: 5xx 3.8% (baseline 0.2%)
Started: ~5m ago
Dash: https://console.redwood.example/ops/dashboards/hosted?route=chat-prod&region=us-east-1
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/ENG/hosted-rollout-pause-and-rollback-runbook

Sean Gallagher: jumping in. seeing spike in `gateway.upstream_5xx` + `model_backend_5xx` for that route. anyone know if there was a config change?

Allison Grant: change feed shows rollout edit ~10 min ago on that route. candidate weight looks like it went from 10% -> 100%.

Rafael Mendes: :eyes: pulling effective policy. one sec.

Mina Haddad: routing on that route is using weighted variants (new canary path). if it’s 100% candidate, we’re effectively full cutover.

Ravi Menon: do we know candidate model/version? might be wrong artifact or not deployed in us-east-1.

Rafael Mendes: ok, effective routing endpoint returns:
- baseline: `llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2024-09-30` weight=0
- candidate: `llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2024-10-06-quant-int4` weight=100
stickiness: `request_hash(account_id, route_id)`

Sean Gallagher: that would explain it. action: pause rollout / force 0% candidate.

Dylan Brooks: I can’t tell if this was user-driven or console auto-step. checking audit timeline.

Jordan Lee: if it’s 100% and guardrails weren’t set, policy engine still accepts it (currently) as long as weights sum to 100. we talked about adding validation to prevent “instant 100%” without admin perms.

Allison Grant: metrics: candidate p95 jumped, then error. looks like backend returning `MODEL_NOT_READY` in us-east-1 for a subset, then retries -> 5xx.

Mina Haddad: could also be region partial capacity for that quant profile. do we have it provisioned everywhere?

Ravi Menon: I’m checking routing logs. seeing a lot of `no_healthy_upstream` for candidate in us-east-1 only.

Dev Patel: support ping: customer Northbridge AI is reporting “all requests failing” on chat-prod. they’re asking if we’re down.

Sean Gallagher: please tell them we’re mitigating now and to retry in a few mins. don’t mention internals yet.

Dev Patel: ack. will respond with “degraded route, mitigation in progress, ETA <10m”.

Rafael Mendes: applying mitigation per runbook: set candidate weight 0 + pause rollout.

Rafael Mendes: (via admin tool) `rollouts pause --route chat-prod --reason "incident mitigation"`
then `rollouts set-weights --baseline 100 --candidate 0`

Incident Bot: Change detected: rollout `rlt_8b19c` paused by Rafael Mendes (reason: incident mitigation)

Allison Grant: watching 5xx now… dropping. currently 1.1% and falling.

Mina Haddad: good. confirm propagation to us-east-1 data plane.

Ravi Menon: seeing policy version bump `v=4182` in router within ~20s. weights now baseline-only.

Sean Gallagher: great. keep an eye for another 5-10 mins. also need to understand how it got to 100%.

Dylan Brooks: audit log shows actor = customer api key `northbridge-prod-admin` via Console. event: `rollout.updated` with schedule step “Promote to 100%”.
looks like they clicked “Next step” twice quickly (?)

Chloe Martin: our UI has a confirmation dialog for “100% candidate” but if their rollout had no guardrails, it still lets them proceed. there’s also a bug where the stepper defaults to 100% when you edit schedule after creating (we have a ticket but not fixed).

Jordan Lee: also note: policy allowed baseline weight=0, candidate=100 while rollout state still “canary”. we might want a distinct “promote” action w/ extra checks.

Allison Grant: recovery: 5xx back to 0.3%. latency returning to baseline. marking incident mitigated once stable for 10m.

Dev Patel: customer updated. they’re seeing success again. asked for RCA + how to prevent.

Sean Gallagher: follow-up items:
1) add validation: prevent 100% candidate unless (a) guardrails present OR (b) explicit “promote” permission.
2) routing: if candidate has no healthy upstream in region, should auto-fallback to baseline instead of hard 5xx (at least for Hosted).
3) docs/support: guidance on not jumping to 100% without verifying candidate readiness.

Mina Haddad: +1 on fallback. we already have fallback for “capacity constrained”; we should treat `no_healthy_upstream` similarly when rollout is active.

Ravi Menon: careful w/ streaming sessions though—fallback mid-stream is messy. but for request start selection, we can fallback to baseline if candidate has zero endpoints.

Allison Grant: creating follow-up ticket? need owner.

Sean Gallagher: I’ll file a linear under canary GA epic. tagging Console + Routing + Policy.

Sean Gallagher: filed: https://linear.redwood.example/issue/ENG-8694 “Guardrail/validation + safe fallback for 0-healthy candidate during Hosted rollout”
assigned initial triage to @Jordan Lee and @Ravi Menon, cc @Dylan Brooks.

Dylan Brooks: thanks. I’ll also spin a smaller Console-specific bug ticket for the schedule editor defaulting to 100% (I think that’s the immediate footgun).

Chloe Martin: please include audit log context + repro steps if you have them. we can try to reproduce with rapid clicks + slow network.

Rafael Mendes: incident notes added in oncall log. mitigation steps used runbook link above. confirming rollback complete.

Incident Bot: Status update: `HOSTED-5XX` moved to *Mitigated* by Sean Gallagher

Allison Grant: will keep dashboards open; so far stable.

Dev Patel: I’ll attach ENG-8694 to the support ticket and let customer know we’ll share a write-up + preventative changes.

Sean Gallagher: closing thread unless it regresses. thanks all.
